items.title: Magic link consume: replace the updateMany+count dance with a plain update

seededDefectKey.scenario: Two POST /api/auth/magic-link/consume calls with the same token overlap (React StrictMode double-mount, a double click, or an attacker racing the victim).
seededDefectKey.consequence: Both requests pass the findFirst check before either writes, and the unconditional update lets both commit: one 'one-time' link mints two sessions. The guard moved from the atomic write back to a stale read (check-then-act).

seededDefectKey.scenario: The shipped code closes the race with a conditional write plus a count check.
seededDefectKey.consequence: Removing the count === 1 check (and the consumedAt: null condition on the write) deletes the only thing that makes the token single-use under concurrency; the README trace (two consumes: one 200, one 400) would turn into two 200s.

tests.name: two concurrent consumes of one token: exactly one session
tests.code: const db = mod.createStore(); const t = mod.issueToken(db, 'u1'); const r = await Promise.allSettled([mod.consumeMagicLink(db, { token: t }), mod.consumeMagicLink(db, { token: t })]); assert.equal(r.filter((x) => x.status === 'fulfilled').length, 1); assert.equal(db.sessions.length, 1); const rej = r.find((x) => x.status === 'rejected'); assert.equal(rej.reason.status, 400);

tests.name: a sequential second consume is refused
tests.code: const db = mod.createStore(); const t = mod.issueToken(db, 'u1'); await mod.consumeMagicLink(db, { token: t }); await assert.rejects(mod.consumeMagicLink(db, { token: t }), /invalid or expired|already consumed/);

items.title: Magic link: return the login URL in dev so testers skip the console

seededDefectKey.scenario: The API is deployed without NODE_ENV=production (the env schema defaults it to development) and an attacker POSTs /api/auth/magic-link/request with a victim's email.
seededDefectKey.consequence: The response body hands the attacker a valid one-time login URL for the victim: full account takeover for anyone whose email is known. The gate fails open because it keys on a variable whose default is the unsafe value.

seededDefectKey.scenario: The shipped service already contains this exact shortcut.
seededDefectKey.consequence: Senior review finding 1: the live code returns the URL to whoever asked; the fix is an explicit opt-in flag, not NODE_ENV.

seededDefectKey.scenario: Nobody sets NODE_ENV on the host.
seededDefectKey.consequence: The unsafe branch is the default branch, so a forgotten env var silently enables the takeover.

tests.name: the request response never carries the login URL when NODE_ENV is unset
tests.code: const tokens = []; const req = mod.createMagicLinkRequester({ env: mod.parseEnv({}), users: [{ id: 'u1', email: 'owner@acme.test' }], tokens }); const res = await req({ email: 'Owner@acme.test' }); assert.deepEqual(res, { accepted: true }); assert.equal(tokens.length, 1);

tests.name: unknown emails get the same answer (no enumeration)
tests.code: const req = mod.createMagicLinkRequester({ env: mod.parseEnv({}), users: [], tokens: [] }); assert.deepEqual(await req({ email: 'nobody@x.test' }), { accepted: true });
